summary: @servicetitan/table preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package's package.json declares a preinstall hook that runs setup.mjs. setup.mjs is itself hex-identifier-obfuscated (identifiers like _0x488df8, _0x52943e; wrapper objects aliasing execFileSync/https.get/chmodSync/writeFileSync) and, at npm install time, downloads a pinned Bun runtime tarball from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods the bun binary executable, and invokes it against a sibling file named math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun bytecode bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) whose contents are obfuscated with string-array shuffle and charcode-array decoding (`_0x`-style symbols, a `hc1jfK9` decoder over a large numeric/char literal table). The Bun runtime executes this opaque payload on the installer's machine as a side effect of `npm install`. The advertised purpose of the package is a React table library, which has no need for an alternate JavaScript runtime or for executing an obfuscated non-source bundle at install time; the file naming (`math_init.js`) is unrelated to any table/UI functionality. Executing the Bun runtime rather than Node bypasses Node-based install-time scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
